reviews.title: Disappointing Experience With Noom Med’s Prescription Coordination
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with my experience with Noom Med. I paid $387 for the 12-week branded GLP-1 telehealth program, in addition to paying $349 separately to NovoCare for my Wegovy medication. Unfortunately, when I needed help with my prescription, the service fell short of what I expected.

My prescribing doctor messaged me confirming that my prescription had been sent. I relied on that confirmation and waited, only to contact NovoCare myself and discover that the prescription had never actually been sent.

I then reached out to Noom’s care coordination team for help. Instead of investigating the issue and helping resolve it, I was told to contact NovoCare myself. Since then, I’ve repeatedly followed up and have essentially been told to wait, with no meaningful resolution or clear timeline.

The most frustrating part is that I had to discover the problem myself after being given incorrect information, and then had to chase down the very service I’m paying for to get answers.

I understand that delays happen, but there is a difference between an unavoidable delay and being told something has been done when it hasn’t. When a service involves prescription management, communication and accountability matter.

At this point, I’ve lost confidence in Noom Med’s ability to provide reliable care coordination. I’ve requested a refund or other appropriate compensation for this service failure, but I’m still waiting for a satisfactory response.

If I’m paying $387 for telehealth support, I expect more than being told to wait and figure things out myself. I hope Noom improves its communication, accountability, and customer support for patients who depend on this service.

If you don’t log in every single day, and also click “log steps, etcetera” they punish you.

For mental health and sometimes work reasons, people cannot log onto this app even single day and shouldn’t be penalized for that. Excessive screen use is also known to impact mental health. 

To penalize people for not being obsessed with their screen and not giving at least a 1-3 day grace period to log your steps, etcetera is wrong and trying to force people to be obsessed with the app. 

How can an app whose whole purpose is health through your mental wellbeing be then negatively impacting mental health by trying to force a screen addiction in order to be properly acknowledged for very hard and tasks and then simply erase them for not logging in one day.

reviews.text: Please add an option to disable animated graphics because they interrupt logging and force app restarts. Those graphics are ugly, distracting, useless, and annoying enough to make me consider canceling my subscription to Noom.

reviews.title: Super helpful for me
reviews.text: I have always understood the concept of a calorie deficit to lose weight, but have struggled to put it in action. Noom’s concept of green, yellow, and orange foods, as well as understanding macros has really helped me make smarter decisions. I was able to figure out what foods made me feel full and which ones didn’t work for me. The articles were very informative and the recipes were awesome! It takes daily logging, but it was worth it for me. I almost met my goal weight, but met so many others (off my statin and pre diabetes meds, and dropped 3 pants sizes) that weight became less important.

reviews.title: Really ended up loving it
reviews.text:
My kids shared this app and the first couple of days I thought it was stupid. Then, once I got into the flow of it, I fell in love with it! I've lost 14 pounds in 3-1/2 months, and have just a couple more to go. But I'll be using this app for the rest of my life. I'm totally geeked, lol. 
It's super easy, has re- shaped my whole relationship with food (reshaped my body too!), and is a great resource.

reviews.title: This works!
reviews.text:
We are in a time where everyone is jumping on the shot bandwagon. I almost jumped, too. BUT instead my husband signed up for Noom. I joined him.  Our son lost 55 lbs on Noon last year. He’s maintaining  really well on Noon. He also inspired us. This is working for us! Philosophically, it really helps for us to curb our eating, have a stronger awareness of how food impacts our health, and how quickly this has impacted our lives. I started 45 days ago. I’ve lost 18.9 lbs as of this morning! My husband has lost 13 lbs. 
We are excited every morning to check our weight loss. We are excited for our future! 
Thank you Noom! 
Betsy

reviews.title: Inspired and encouraged
reviews.text: Noom has been a source of inspiration and encouragement when I had given up keeping my weight in check. I love the fact that there is not such a thing as a bad and evil food group and the sense that I will achieve my goal sooner or later. I don’t feel rushed or defeated after a pizza night with the family. It’s so easy to regain momentum the following day. Noom is a game changer!

And just to balance, the photo meal scanning works surprisingly well. I’m glad it does not save to camera roll.

reviews.title: Excellent Choice
reviews.text:
I used Noom about 4-5 years ago. List 30-35 lbs and was thrilled. Have recommended it to friends and family members. My niece lost 20 lbs and her mother (so far) has lost 56 lbs). 

I recently went thru a rough patch and gained 14-15 lbs (depending on the day) so I rejoined. I already know I will be a lifetime member once I’m at goal which is fast approaching.  I cannot give enough positive feedback about this program. Do yourself a favor and- try it. You’ll like it and be VERY happy either way the results.

reviews.title: It’s working
reviews.text: Am I enjoying it?  I’m not sure. But I am losing weight and somehow still interested to continue with it. There are some good techniques read by someone who is just reading things off of a card unexcitedly! Also the app forgets to connect to my steps on my phone, refuses to connect to “my air” for my CPAP machine to tell me how my sleep effects things, and sometimes forgets the food I’ve saved. However the most important thing is that I’m losing weight and am not hungry!

reviews.title: Chat bot hell
reviews.text: If you have an issue you’ll be sent to the worst possible chatbot with no other options.

reviews.title: Expensive for a tracker
reviews.text: I am using Noom Med to get access to GLP-1, which has been fine. But the app itself is expensive for AI generated content. Also, your “clinician” is a group of nurse practitioners around the world who don’t read your chat conversation and you end up having to answer the same questions over and over just to get a refill or new prescription. It’s incredibly frustrating to go back and forth with several “clinicians” who clearly just read the last message I sent and not the conversation. Also I’m pretty sure my “coach” is AI even though it claims to be human when I ask. If you’re able to get GLP-1s somewhere else that doesn’t cost as much, go that route first.

reviews.title: App stopped working and no options to request refund
reviews.text:
Update to the update - finally got a hold of someone who instructed me to update the app (I guess it didn’t happen automatically) and that fixes the activity tracker issue for a few weeks. Now it is down again 😭

Update - App stopped grabbing active minutes from my Apple Watch two weeks ago, which made the meal tracking portion of the app useless. I spent over an hour talking with their chat bot on three separate occasions trying to troubleshoot the source of the issues and they were never able to get to the root of it or fix it. I asked for a refund and the link they sent led to a defunct page. So now although I have paid for the app for several more months, there is no option for a refund and no solution in site. See below for earlier recommendations on how to make the app better but most of all - give people a refund if your software stops working. 
1. Separate recipes from meals - they are different
2. Add a scan function when creating a recipe. It is so annoying and tedious to have to type out every item in a recipe and weird that I can’t just scan some ingredients.
3. Make it possible to upload recipes either from a cook book or website - with scan to text possible it seems slow and clunky that I have to hand type a recipe (and some of them are long!). This easily adds 10-15 minutes to my meal logging time. 
4. Please add an option to show protein amounts and other macro data for my recipes and meals. If it isn’t my first meal of the day I write down what my protein is and then do math 
5. Would love a fiber tracking component - I’ve had to focus so much on adding protein to my diet (lots of dairy since I’m veg) and am worried I’m sacrificing fiber - especially since I read recently that most Americans don’t get enough fiber.
6. Can you have the app remember my favorite foods and/or improve the search function. I eat a lot of 4% Organic Valley Cottage Cheese but if I don’t type it in exactly right the app cannot find it. I know I can scan it but sometimes I’m not in front of the fridge when I’m logging my food.

reviews.title: So Helpful
reviews.text: I really like the changes that have been made to the app. It's so much more engaging and I really look forward do opening it now. My only request it to have a "favorites" function where I can mark foods I eat regularly so I don't have to type them in all the time.

reviews.title: Warning For Late Night Workers
reviews.text:
I often work late (home just before 12am), and it is highly frustrating that there is not at LEAST a 1hr or so grace period to finish logging things for the day. This app is not accommodating or considerate that some of its users may be late night workers/night shift. I am unable to use my phone while working, so this is particularly frustrating and distressing for me. In some of the lessons they discuss the importance of mental wellness, and the lack of flexibility is not helping mine. 
I think that the app should include a setting for those of us who have a late night work schedule. I’m very disappointed with this fact, and whenever I am unable to log my accomplishments I feel like a failure (not good for the mental wellness upon which multiple lessons put great emphasis). 
HIGHLY considering discontinuing using this app/program due to the lack of consideration and lack of even minor accommodations that late night workers need.

reviews.title: Noom feels like a friend
reviews.text: Noom’s first daily lessons gave me a jump start asking why I really want to lose weight then small steps to build on for lifelong success.  It’s like they read my mind on what I need to succeed.

reviews.title: Weight Loss App for Phone Addicts
reviews.text: Finally an app with AI that makes it so quick and easy to track calories going in and figures out the proper blend of food groups. The app is full of recipes and activities and rewards to keep me engaged. Just finished my first week and shed 5 lbs without feeling hangry (some of that is water weight).

reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.text: Noom is nothing more than a click app to make you feel like you are doing something. It acts like Facebook, with community- who need another app to compare yourself with others? The app gives no personal help everything is just system generated for a set plan nothing is individualized. Eat 3000 calories great job! Skip all you meals great work! Your coach is going to just going to tell you the same scripted message with the same positive feedback. Now they want you too add friends and have your friends waste their money as well. This is just a Ponzi scheme to get ppl to not use and collect money. They just added a "seed" program where you "donate" to charities but no actual charities listed & you can only choose from a limited genre. If I did not have to use this to get my diabetic medicine for my health plan I would not use it.  Have I lost any weight- no because I was already doing all their "tips" and there is nothing more to change. Can I personalize how to use this- no you can't decrease calories, or make anything personalized. Even the lessons have a generalized plan you must go through, most of which do not apply specifically to me. If you want to keep up appearances use this app, if you want to change your life & loose weight- paper, pen, a calorie counting app and AI is much cheaper. By the way telling people "there is no bad food" but then ranking food by color is saying there is bad food.

reviews.title: Good, but obnoxious notifications
reviews.text: I’ve used this app off and on for quite a few years now, both paid and unpaid versions. Overall it’s a great app and easy to prioritize to your health goals. My one big issue is the absolutely obnoxious number of notifications. It’s currently 8pm and since 7:30 this morning I’ve received 12 notifications. There’s no option to reduce that number in-app, so you either have to turn all notifs off, or deal with an hourly reminder to do something or other. Please, let me have just one notification a day to remind me to log my meals. Some folks might like the heavy-handed reminders but I want an option for fewer without turning them off entirely.

reviews.title: Was Once a Great App…
reviews.text: But then it was turned into a game and got much more complicated. I gave it three stars, because sure, it still does all of the things it did before, like providing a course to help you lose and track weight, track food and nutrition, and read helpful and supportive articles. But they’ve just added too much, thinking all the extras will motivate, or something. What was once a simple to use app that took very little of your time has been bogged down with daily art and banking seeds? What? Perhaps a better organized or more customizable interface would help, but long and silly animations and too much on the home page make the app less friendly to use. Here’s hoping they figure it out, so I can get back to the daily simplicity they preach in their articles about how to live the best version of yourself.

Foods like Twinkies and Oreos and Doritos and soda and other processed food should be in that category.

reviews.title: Noon used to be good
reviews.text:
Noon helped me lose weight, but it’s become impossible to use. Too many congratulatory screens and hoops to jump through in order to simply log calories. Also, it should be easier to log workouts.

The psychology tests are good but after awhile they can be an annoyance when you just want to log progress. I do like that you can take a picture of your meal and it will break it down by calories but I am concerned how much electrical power is being consumed at data centers nationwide to do that. I use it sparingly because I’m not sure it’s worth it.

The interface should be more simple. Maybe I’ve outgrown it, but it does seem to have the problem all cool software and apps eventually succumb to. Some developer feels the need to add bells & whistles rather than keep it simple and effective.

I thought at the time I could at least keep the food logs for my medical reasons but that was taken from me without warning as well after they changed. I’m incredibly frustrated and do not suggest this to anyone. Choose something else or some other program if you think this might help. Don’t expect a “coach” to help. You can get recipes from online too you don’t need this app.

reviews.title: Too gimmicky
reviews.text:
The app is way too gimmicky. There is no way to customize the app. 

You can’t put in medication foundayo - unless you buy in to the higher tier. So if you want the RX reminder you have to choose one of the offered choices. 

You also can not turn off the annoying “seeds” award part of the app which goes through an annoying song and dance. Sometimes you’re in a hurry and just want to log in your information. 

If you ask for help you’re shuffled to an AI app, which is pretty useless. 

If you’ve been through the articles before, picking and choosing what you need to help would be helpful. 

If you have specific health issues like knee or back then the article information does not match up with your needs. 

Being able to customize the app to your needs would be fantastic; otherwise, it’s an expensive calorie counter.

Recipe library is also pretty mid / doesn’t replace the need to look elsewhere, which is fine. 

One other suggestion would be to add a feature to log how you mentally or physically felt after a meal. Could be helpful to track.

It just seems silly that I track meatballs from Costco by scanning the QR code and then the next day, I don’t have the QR code any longer and when I put in beef meatballs, it doesn’t show up.  It will give me 87 beef meatball options of which I haven’t used. The one I used recently should be at the top of the list. Or have an eaten recently section.  At the top of my list before I log anything, it says frittata because I ate that one time  many years ago.  Why not list the food I’ve eaten recently?

reviews.title: Things I love, things I hate, suggestions for improvement
reviews.text: I love the app. It provides robust education and tracking tools. I appreciate the integration with my activity trackers. And then the adjustment of my daily calorie budget. I find the macro nutrients data and education very useful. I definitely recommend the app. What I do not like are what seem like manipulative sales tactics to get people to sign up for the app. The app is wonderful and being honest and straightforward and transparent will sell the app. Trust your product and create simple transparent pricing. One wish list feature: I’d love a feature that lets me take a photo of my plate after eating and subtract the remaining food from the meal I logged earlier. That would make photo logging much more accurate when I don’t finish everything.

reviews.title: D&L Family

reviews.title: Very effective tool for weight loss and improving health
reviews.text: I have used NOOM successfully to lose close to 45 pounds. My daughter used it as well very successfully after having had 3 children. It’s very basic in its approach, calories in and calories out. If you use the food log diligently and get your body moving more such that you stay within the weight loss range of intake, no doubt you will be successful in losing weight. The addition of inspiring advice and mental boosts to maintain a positive attitude, stress reduction and nutrition guidance are all really great. It does provide a really excellent framework to develop better habits for eating and exercise. I highly recommend this app. My daughter and I have both kept the weight off for a good long stretch now by sticking with the new habits we developed. Additionally, I enjoy a wide wide variety of treats (croissants, ice cream, pastries, pop corn, chips, etc) as long as they fit into the overall framework of more calories out than taken in. Moderation is key and they really should be treats on occasion to make them special. Not everyday events.

reviews.title: It’s making weight loss fun
reviews.text: I’m like addicted to logging stuff in this little app, and not in like a OCD way. I don’t have social media so this app is my digital dopamine hit. reviews.title: Encouraging

I’ve lost close to four pounds in a month and it makes me want to keep going. I wanted sustainable weight loss without drugs. So far, Noom is working for me.

reviews.title: Avoid this Program
reviews.text:
My onboarding experience with Noom’s medical weight loss program has been incredibly disappointing.
I enrolled hoping to receive an oral weight loss medication, but the prescribing provider mistakenly prescribed an injectable medication instead. I immediately reached out to have the error corrected, but it’s now been over two weeks, and I still haven’t heard back from the doctor despite sending multiple messages.
I’ve also contacted Noom’s support team several times. While they’ve been polite, they’ve repeatedly told me they can’t reach the prescribing provider or resolve the issue themselves. As a result, I’ve been stuck paying for a service I haven’t been able to use.
To make matters worse, Noom has refused to refund the $150 I paid, even though the issue was caused by an incorrect prescription on their end.
Mistakes happen, but what concerns me most is the complete lack of communication and accountability. If you’re considering Noom’s medical weight loss program, I’d strongly recommend looking at other options where providers are responsive and customer support is actually empowered to help when something goes wrong.

reviews.title: Longtime Subscriber
reviews.text: I have been using Noom daily for quite some time. I feel it offers excellent guidance and tracking ability for everything that I eat. I do feel that the latest incarnations are way over complicated and built too much to look like a game. I’m really not interested in animations and seeds or banking anything, I’m just interested in logging my food and keeping up on my hydration, exercise and basic health. Please keep it simple- now there are so many options, it’s becoming work, where it used to be a pleasure. At the very least, maybe offer a “classic” version for those of us who don’t need the constant animations and affirmations. For what it’s worth, my weight fluctuates a lot because of medication and thyroid disease, so while I would like to say I’ve had tons of success with Noom, that wouldn’t be true but it’s not because of the program. It’s because of my health, that’s why I’ve been here for a while and prefer using it just as a tracking and maintenance tool.

reviews.title: Bloatware

If there were an option to subscribe to a stripped down version focused just on food tracking, and weigh-ins I’d sign up in a heart beat. I don’t need the animations, I don’t need to redo the course, and I don’t need ll the extra fluff. I just want a clean, simple way to track what I eat, because that part of the app is genuinely the best I’ve used!

reviews.text:
In 2024 I join NOOM for the second time. I was in such pain from bone on bone in my hip joint & my doctor wouldn’t do hip replacement until I got my BMI down.
I was adamant about getting my weight down so I could have my surgery. And NOOM really helped me to be able to do that. 
I am so grateful that I have NOOM to help me. I got my hip replacement in the beginning of 2025. I’m still losing more weight with NOOM. Every time I walk by a mirror I almost don’t recognize myself. I take a double look.

reviews.title: Too gamified now
reviews.text: This is my second time doing Noom; the first time was a great success, and this time around started off great with a bang. But then an update hit the app a couple of months ago that made it nearly unusable. The gamification has been taken to the extreme and it seems like I can’t log a meal without 5 pop-ups to shower me with affirmation, seeds, and lightning bolts, and then another pop up to encourage me to chase some other token. Noom as a program and a system works; I can follow the system but to do so I need to log meals without it taking an eternity and making me cringe. There should be a setting or settings in the app to disable some of those over-the-top features,  especially for people like me who are not particularly wired psychologically to respond to affirmation and praise, and don’t need gamification and token-seeking to stay motivated. Results motivate me and right now it’s hard to chase those results with an utterly unusable app.

When so many of us are on GLP-1s?Customer service just blows me off on if/when Fiber will will be available.

reviews.title: Color system messing with my feelings of success
reviews.text:
The color system is psychologically misleading. Staying within calorie goals and eating healthy foods can still feel like failure because one color category goes over while another remains underfilled. Unused calories from one category should dynamically redistribute instead of leaving empty sections that visually imply goals weren’t met. The current design feels unintentionally discouraging even on healthy eating days. I feel more guilty for eating a cup of lentils than a chocolate chip cookie because I went over on yellow foods and didn’t fulfill my orange food “goals.” It becomes a psychological issue, which is ironic considering the program is based on psychology.
I also found it surprisingly difficult to access basic information about which foods belong in each color category. I was trying to figure out whether a snack fit within my goals and couldn’t readily find the information. It took me two days to finally locate it. When I used the help chat, it sent me links that didn’t work, and after I explained that the links were broken, I just received a generic apology instead of actual help. That was incredibly frustrating. Information this important should be much easier for users to access since the entire program revolves around staying within these categories and calorie goals.
At this point, I’m not sure this is the right weight loss app for me.

reviews.title: Useful but has may functional and UX issues
reviews.text:
The app has many solid features for calorie, step, habit tracking, etc. I like the data aspect of it. 

The calorie tracker throughout the day is not a linear scale. The last ~250 calories or so are a huge portion of the scale and can be misleading. Let us adjust this! 

There are SO many full screen animations. I’m able to turn off some of the seed reward ones. I just want to log my weight and enter my breakfast without having to either wait for an animation to complete or quit the app and restart between them. Let us turn these off, PLEASE, or just make them less invasive banners. 

Can’t seem to create a custom food/meal with specific macros.

Food search works well, but recent foods are not grouped to the top intelligently. If I ate something for lunch one day, maybe I’d want to have that in recents for dinner as well, or at least have it appear near the top of a similar search.

It's a fine tool and the lessons are good to keep in mind but if you're just looking for a calorie counter, there are better, cheaper options.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
“Psychology based” so long as your answers to quizzes fit the ones they provide, I guess.

I am currently at a fairly healthy weight, but I’m struggling with an impulse control issue. Given that Noom talks about using psychology to address eating patterns, I figured I’d give it a try. I deleted it before the free trial period ended. 

First, it threw me off to be offered probiotics before the app knew anything about me. I guess it just assumes everyone should be buying that product. I don’t need it, so it felt like a profit center more than sound nutritional advice. 

The bigger issue was that the app didn’t give me the opportunity to adequately explain my situation. My impulse control issue is related to ADHD. I’ve always struggled with it, but I was just diagnosed as having ADHD about 18 months ago. Unfortunately, I’m allergic to the stimulants that best treat ADHD. I’m currently on a non-stimulant prescription. It’s nowhere near as effective, and I’m back to having frequent evening binge eating sessions. I was hopeful Noom would help me address this behavior and give me workable solutions. 
The first issue came up with the quizzes. I encountered questions for which none of the given answers were even close, and there was no option to choose “other” or to write my own answer. 
I tried to use the help function. I got the AI bot. It asked me to upload a screenshot. I am a competent iPhone user, and I could not find a way to upload a screenshot. The bot told me it would connect me with a coach. I waited several minutes. I then replied “I can’t keep waiting on a response as I have other things I need to do.” 
I tried again, but I ran into the same issue with quizzes. Same runaround with the bot. 
Several days later, I found a bunch of emails in my junk mail folder. Tech support had contacted me by email. I didn’t know they had, so I didn’t go looking for an email. 
I replied even though I’d already deleted the app. I explained my situation with the quiz answers that are available didn’t match my situation at all, and that the bot wanted me to upload a screenshot but I couldn’t see how to do it. They replied, telling me that sounded like something that needed to be addressed by a coach… 
I imagine the stock answers the app allows a user to choose work for the majority of people. I’m not one of them, though.

reviews.title: Bad for so many reasons
reviews.text: I kept getting ads for this app so I tried it out. Immediately I’m bombarded with their internal advertising about their GLP-1 program and that should have already raised red flags for me. However, I continued with it as I wanted to know the “change your mindset about food” lessons. All I got was an arbitrary food rating system that not only was super inconsistent (like saying bananas was a “green” food while beans are a “yellow” food due to its higher calorie density even though bananas are about the same caloric density as beans) but as someone who had an ED for many years all it did was bring me back into the mindset where I would not even touch certain foods due to it not being a “green” food. The AI generated help was also pretty awful, basically saying my weight loss plateau was because I’m not eating enough “green” foods and that I should incorporate them in my diet. Unless you want to eat like a rabbit living off of spinach and arugula, anyone with a working body and a brain would know that’s impossible on a nutrition standpoint. Coaches were also super unhelpful not giving specific help on the questions you had. Most of the time, it sounded just as bad as the AI help or even worse like they’re just reading from a prompt. So if you want to spend money to obsess over food in an unhealthy manner, get advice that somehow is even worse than ChatGPT, and basically get the marketing that “oh this app is so good…..if you join our medication program!” then be my guest to spend an ungodly amount of money for the most terrible food tracking app I’ve ever used. If I can give negative stars on this I would

reviews.title: Very frustrating to use
reviews.text:
In some of the lessons there are suggestions to look up and find foods that are healthy to eat more of, and seem to imply you should bookmark them for later so you don’t forget. But there is no way to do so. 
There are workout videos on the app and filters to look for workouts based on intensity, workout equipment, area to focus on, etc. But they don’t work. And after clicking to look at the details of one workout, all the filters are gone and you have to start over. (I tried asking their ai bot and it eventually told me to report the issue from the FAQ page. But the links it provided were all non-functioning links)
If you want to add a recipe so you can easily track eating it later, you have to first go in like you are going to track a meal now. And if you have added a number of items but swipe the wrong way, you’ll loose everything and have to start over again. 
While some of the information in the lessons seems very sound, there are some things that I wouldn’t trust without double checking a reputable source. It’s possible I learned or remembered things incorrectly, but since I don’t know the credentials and work/research history of their doctors, they may know every well what they are talking about. But I don’t know. 
Trainer guidance is super vague and not particularly helpful either.

Any recipe featured should be loaded into recipes (which would enhance that offering) and have calories and log capability. Oversight that needs to be corrected!

reviews.title: Surprisingly effective!
reviews.text: This was a bit of a shot in the dark. My husband did research on Noom and was impressed by what he found but we were conscious it was a financial investment. Roughly 6 weeks later, I have lost 4 lbs and my husband has lost 5 lbs. It has been gradual, with fluctuation. However, it has worked so far! I think Noom is great because it is holistic and gives you long-term, sustainable methods for losing weight. You don’t cut out any food groups, you treat yourself occasionally and focus on a balance of healthy foods, calorie management, and exercise. Most importantly, it reframes your view of nutrition and weight loss. I highly recommend Noom to anyone interested in long term, healthy, and sustainable weight loss!

reviews.title: Please get rid of haptics!
reviews.text:
While Noom has come a long way, the inability to override haptics via Noom and iPhone settings is extremely annoying. The vibrations when logging anything are jarring. While some might view this as minor, I feel when paying for an app, we should have control of these things. 

Another point of annoyance- the inability to scan labels when  adding recipe ingredients. Scanning is available for logging. Why not for recipe building? 

After briefly trying Noom Med twice (under a different account), and being assigned two different coaches, there was a glaring difference: one coach reached out often. The other didn’t reach out for 10 days. Inconsistency for this feature was glaring. 

Food color look up: You can scan a barcode or type in a food and see the same food entered as every color. It’s frustrating and not helpful. 

Price: each time I have been on Noom, pricing is always inconsistent. Sometimes I’m charged monthly, sometimes several months all at once. Sometimes there are discounted pricing, sometimes not. When canceling, I’ve been offered a lower rate to stay— why not offer the lower rate to begin with?

I’d like to also say that I was loving this app prior.  I’ve lost over 40 pounds, I literally use it every day, and I loved it up until this update. I would’ve given it five stars.  Now I’m just frustrated, Noom hasn’t updated any of the health articles to align with the new functionality, so I can’t even figure out what’s going on. Their support/help indicates that coins still exist, all I see are seeds (which are again incredibly annoying).

reviews.title: Too many gimmicks
reviews.text: App update adds seeds and other gimmicks which are annoying and unnecessary. Treat people like adults.

reviews.title: Didn’t Like
reviews.text: My Fitness Pal was easier to use. Noom doesn’t have many foods saved in the calorie counting section. I had to manually enter almost everything. The app was not enjoyable.

reviews.title: Noom- Work the Program!
reviews.text: Noom works IF you work the program. You don’t have to do everything offered, just the most important parts…daily weigh in, booking food intake, step counter, plus the 10 minute daily lessons will change how you see food…IT WORKS! It evens out the highs & lows of weight loss to keep you motivated and on the right track even when you fall to temptation.

reviews.title: Easy to use
reviews.text: Great for logging food and patterns

reviews.title: No longer useful
reviews.text: I used and successfully lost 30 lbs with noom several years ago. Decided to get back into it and the app has completely changed to be about selling you GLP-1s? It used to be excellent at teaching you the psychology around weight and weight loss and how to fit it into your lifestyle so it would stick. I recommended it to everyone. Now you can’t even log a meal without paying and they have farmed most of the features out to poor AI. I feel like selling weight loss drugs is also completely contrary to the original intent which was about sustainable lifestyle changes

reviews.title: Never too old to learn
reviews.text: I was needing to lose weight for my health and I’m 63 closest to 64 years old. I thought I knew what there was to know about food but getting new I have learned so much in the last month. It has been a big help. Not only if I learned about food I have learned a lot about protein and what’s needed in the body, even at my age and how to train my mind on how and when to eat. I love Noom.

reviews.title: Not for meds
reviews.text: The tracker is fine, not the best at finding restaurant foods and the feature where you take a picture of your plate works better on other sites.  The real problem is Noom med - the help-1 prescription feature. I interacted with 3 different NPs, each of them was extremely unhelpful. They did not look at my chart and they asked for documentation that I was not prepared ahead of time with. For example, if I'd known in advance that they wanted my most recent labs, I would have had them available right then.  When I asked questions about the process or program they seemed confused.

reviews.title: Love app
reviews.text: I like the app cause it’s like going to Weightwatchers, you weigh in , describe your food and have options and have a person or AI to talk to if needed! It’s worth a try! Accountability is everything to me!

reviews.title: Good program
reviews.text: Good way to keep track and be mindful of calories. Body scans are interesting and the glp program is also an added bonus along with support in chats with Noom coach and doctors

reviews.title: Deceptive
reviews.text:
I signed up for the app with my husband. Plan for both of us was .50 for a one week trial
After one week basic plan will be charged at 338.00/10 months, healthy aging 29.00/10 months and premium 74.25/10 months
We like the app and it was pretty cool that my husband a plan together they didn't offer this before.

The problem is on the day that I signed up for the plan I logged in and they offered me a discount. They said we will refund your $.50 trial that you paid immediately today. I would pay pay $253.50 instead of the $338. A savings of 25%.

I accepted that and expected a charge right away on my PayPal. That didn't happen.

So for two days now, I have been trying to find somebody to help me. I have been getting all sorts of discount offers like 20% off of a basic plan if you take your husband off. This makes absolutely no sense. Why would I take my husband off of a plan that we both want to work with. Somebody else said he he's gonna try to help - he's a supervisor but he has to escalate it because it might be a glitch in their system. 
All I know is that for Noom they are offering many different prices and almost feel like they are doing something questionable with the pricing. 
There's no upfront pricing when you go and look at Noom anywhere. Buyer beware. I enjoy the program. I lost a lot of weight on the program but this runaround with the pricing is just crazy. 
I got Noom for $99  when I first signed up several years ago -?I left because every single time I renewed, the price went up.

reviews.title: Noom Med
reviews.text: Bad experience. The meds work but the customer service is horrible. They have 4 different channels within the app and sometimes they point you to an email as well - the people on the email will point you back to the app who will point you to the email and so on. Nobody knows anything about the product or supports any issues.

reviews.title: Meal logging
reviews.text:
I wish there were other options for tracking meals vs breakfast, morning snack, lunch, etc. 
I often have a preworkout snack, an after workout protein shake, & then a few hours later I have breakfast. 
It’s not a huge deal since the end result is to track the calories etc. Just a thought for a more accurate look into someone’s day.

reviews.title: Dangerous service
reviews.text: I have never written a review of an app, but my experience with Noom was so awful, I feel compelled to so that others are warned. Noom provided me with inaccurate information many times (dangerous since I had a prescription with them) and overcharged me. There is no one to speak to in person, and it took many messages when something serious occurred to get a proper response. It is egregious that they are allowed to provide prescriptions since no one on their client care or customer service team is able to provide accurate information. Only the doctor was helpful.

reviews.title: Billing is a scam- app is fun Weight loss (2# in 2 wks) not impressive even with meds
reviews.text:
I’ve been at a weight loss plateau for four or five months so I tried the new the free Noom app.
I still didn’t lose weight and I was tired of being stuck so I decided to try the four week $99 promotion.
The app was fun. The macro tracking was great. The coach was a sweetheart. After two weeks, they billed me early for the next four weeks. I had to talk to three people to cancel that and as soon as I did, they canceled my access to the full Noom app.
So I am on medication without medical support and without the app that I paid for for four weeks.

It doesn’t make any sense. The “auto turn-off” mechanism needs to be adjusted to the 4 weeks I paid for & not queued to the early billing cycle (that’s set 2 whole weeks early!) (it’s probably so they can order & ship the meds, but it’s certainly not a reason to rip off subscribers. I might have gone back to it in future if I needed it but, now? No way. 
Unfair Business Practices 
It’s really an easy fix that the company needs to implement.

That said - logging my food on Noom has been a great experience & I would recommend it to get anyone started on their health quest!!

reviews.title: Subscription only now
reviews.text: I revisited Noom after a hiatus to try and balance my caloric intake. Now you can only enter food and weight for the current day. You cannot view your previous meals in detail. The help chat has no information and told me they were unaware (you should be able to do this) but could not help me further. They suggested I delete and redownload the app, which I did and it still doesn’t work. Disappointed and now looking for a different app to track my calories. I am super bummed since this app helped me lose 25 lbs 5 years ago.

reviews.title: Ripoff
reviews.text: They do not send meds on time, charge you and then make impossible to get in touch with anybody to rectify the situation. 0 stars

reviews.title: Paywalled their calorie tracker
reviews.text:
I used to love it, they used to offer an awesome calorie tracker and limited it so it’s paywalled impractical. Sketchy data practices. 

Can’t figure out how to delete my account/data - they can spam me but my email isn’t working w the password reset. 

Sad to see a great app/service fall into the dark side of user patterns and arbitrary limitation of the free tier.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.text: I am really enjoying the Noom app and have recommended it to family. I enjoy gaining seeds through all the activities you can do in the app and using those seeds to donate to different causes or eventually get a gift card.

reviews.title: Not worth paying for
reviews.text:
I tried Noom two years ago. I appreciated some of the concepts and especially the accountability of logging food. 
Some of the lessons were borderline offensive or just lost me because the wording was too folksy and talking down to their customers. Plus I almost never had time to look at them until after midnight, which was not the end of my day.
The food logging became a real hassle with lots of popular brands and items not in the database or in there but incorrect. They were happy to have paying customers do their work for them by manually logging information which the system then deleted, EVERY TIME. I had to constantly re-enter items that I had frequently and didn’t have time to do that every time. Plus they lumped all higher fat foods together so avocado was in the same food category as Twinkies. Ridiculous.  The system was also extremely unforgiving with spelling and names. Another hassle.
It also forced me to send Noom emails to friends or family but no one wants to get those emails lol. That was so dumb and another hassle.

I didn’t agree that daily weigh-ins desensitized members to being weighed. It’s excessive and wastes time.
It also did not work to transfer my steps and exercise from another app. 
I lost a quarter of my goal and quit Noom after about 4 months because it was too annoying and I felt it focused too much on calories and eating certain foods. They had some good information but it got lost in the tedium of the rest of the app. You don’t need to pay a bunch of money for that information. 
I see they’re now cashing in on the GLP-1 craze. SO MUCH FOR THEIR TAGLINE ABOUT JUST CHANGING YOUR RELATIONSHIP WITH FOOD.

reviews.title: Was Perfect… Until They Added the Subscription
reviews.text: I have been on Noom since 2018 and have been able to lose much weight with their calorie tracking feature. I recently redownloaded the app, and found out now you have to pay ≈$200 every 3 months to use the program. Who has that kind of money? I only want to use the app for the calorie logging feature, and now it costs so much. It is inaccessible for those unable to pay. Other calorie logging apps are not nearly as well organized as Noom, which is why I am not reviewing 1 star. This app is great, but now it is no longer a helpful program, and rather a commodity being sold.

reviews.title: Why did I wait so long?!
reviews.text: I’ve been using Noom for almost a month now and I have learned so much about my eating habits, and I’m improving my body image. I’ve lost 8lbs so far.

reviews.title: App should track across multiple devices
reviews.text: I’ve diligently been using your App since March 5. On upgraded my iPhone on April 1 and all data and Apps from my old device migrated successfully to my new iPhone EXCEPT my Noom data. Your technical support team advises that this has been an issue when someone changes devices in the middle of their membership and there is reportedly nothing that they can do. My daily history cannot be restored, so I lost one month of diligent daily recording. Curiously, your App didn’t lose my payment information….and when the next subscription payment will be due. Your technology is quite disappointing.

reviews.title: Free App Disappointing
reviews.text: I’ve been using Noom for 6+ years and paid for subscriptions which I enjoyed, yet during times when I didn’t need a paid subscription, the free version was a great support system to let me keep tracking my weight, my meals/calories, and my steps. Very disappointed that the new version doesn’t allow me to keep logging my daily weigh ins, that I cannot type in my food journal, and does not show me calorie tracker. You’ve sidelined a group of people who listened to the education and continue to use the app as a good habit, and you took away access to my data that I’ve been using to maintain a healthy and active lifestyle. I’m disappointed that now those basic features are now behind a very expensive subscription with more bells and whistles than needed this time. Bring back the basic free features!

reviews.title: Love it!!
reviews.text: This is a really good app and it does pay out rewards

reviews.title: What a joke
reviews.text: I tried Noom Med (the app plus compounded semaglutide/GLP-1) and it was an awful experience. They hooked me with an affordable first month and then $268/month for 3 months, but they take payment up front (3 months in one payment), and once they have your money they abandon you. I was having side effects and the doctor would take days to respond to my questions about what to do/dose adjustments. The app was okay, kinda glitchy, and felt more AI than personal. I don’t recommend.

reviews.title: Healthy choices
reviews.text: Having been on Noom for almost a month I have lost a considerable amount of weight and by staying committed I’m able to make healthy food choices, and improving my health considerably at the same time. I feel great.

reviews.title: How the mighty have fallen
reviews.text: I’ve used the program before and was great but it seems to have gotten too big for the developer and team to keep up with.  Meal logging is frustrating at best, imposible at worst.  They rely on users to populate the food list but it’s almost always inaccurate.  When I voice this the answer is “ we know it can be frustrating, but try entering items yourself”.    Not helpful.

reviews.title: Poor quality all around
reviews.text: I had done compound semaglutide through a compound pharmacy directly and loved it. Wanted to try this company for the convenience. Do not waste your money! It did not work and is super hard to cancel

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: Really unimpressed - glad I didn’t pay for it (insurance covered it). The color coding based just on calorie density seems like a very one-dimensional approach. The worst part, by far, is the food logging system - the database is really lacking, and trying to add something yourself to use again the future is just terrible. Describing the meal is worthless (describe a chicken meal from a restaurant, etc., something common even, and it tries to put that you’re eating an entire chicken). It tries to motivate you and talks about having difficulty with the program that manifests in not logging meals or going to the app, but I’m not using the app as much because I dread trying to use the meal log.

reviews.title: Please do better.
reviews.text: This app is the worst. It doesn’t play well with other apps. It glitches and freezes ALL THE TIME. It doesn’t recognize some of the most common foods.

reviews.title: App good - live people so so
reviews.text: The app is really good. The interaction with live people can be frustrating because it’s hard to get a straight answer to questions. Ping pong referrals to different areas for answers.

reviews.title: Pretty good could be better
reviews.text:
First time using the app. Tracking helps awareness and intention which helps me make better choices. That is good.
For better learning for me I wish the food-lookup included the protein not just the “color” and calories. I am trying to learn and do better for life long changes.

reviews.title: Learn how to lose the weight
reviews.text: Noom is a fantastic app to use for help understanding weight loss. The food tracker and nutritional database are robust and easy to use. The recipes and nutritional guidance tell you what are the healthiest foods to choose. The available lessons aid in understanding your relationship to food so it can be improved and you can get the weight off and keep it off.

reviews.title: They ruined the app
reviews.text: Used to be easy to use now the new and improved version is hard to use and you spend a lot of time trying to just enter information and trying to find the place to enter info. The menus are not user friendly

reviews.title: Love the help app experience not great
reviews.text: The weight loss program is great and how it helps you is fantastic. But the app experience and functionality is not fantastic. Like if i want to log one of their meals they have I can log it and get total calories but it won’t log the micros of what color foods it was or how many grams of protein it was, but they provide it in the recipe. I also if i save my own meal it will tell me how many calories and protein I eat but when i log the meal it only logs th cal and 0 protein.

reviews.title: Former WW now sold out to Noom
reviews.text: I LOVE that Noom includes lessons every day that help me learn how to fuel my body. The app is so fun to use and I’m enjoying it, not dreading a “diet”.

reviews.title: Good but not great
reviews.text: Meal log feature REALLY needs improvement. It’s frustrating that the app won’t recognize the colors of each food that you enter manually. I wish they would just allow the app to talk to the LoseIt! App.

reviews.title: Changed the Game For Me
reviews.text: I’m sure just like everyone else we’ve tried it all and it could definitely be a mindset shift this time around but incorporating Noom into my weight loss goal Has made everything so much cleaner clear and easier to do. I find the food tracking is easier than my fitness pal. I love the layout of the app. It’s just all around the best decision I’ve made in 2026.

reviews.title: Betsy2026
reviews.text: Noon has worked where no other diet has.

reviews.title: Beyond expectation!
reviews.text: This program has really helped me get started and to stay on top of both my nutrition and my exercise. The step-by-step explanations in each module are clear and easy to follow, which made the whole experience even better. I couldn’t have asked for a more effective way to kickstart my 61st year of life.

reviews.title: Step count does not work
reviews.text: All of a sudden the step count stopped working. The step goal is set at 5000 however it posts as 0. As of now the app shows 0/0 steps. Everything else works fine, but the step option does not. Very frustrating.

reviews.title: Do some maintenance, please
reviews.text: I spent an hour trying to input a recipe, with no success. Ingredients are limited quantities and measurements, and trying to go back to select a different ingredient removes ALL ingredients one has added. When I finally got everything input, it didn’t save the recipe. I tried to report this bug and got shuffled from one AI to another. I have screenshots now. This is the only way I can think of to get this complaint to you. The app was great when I did Noom a couple years ago. It feels kind of derelict now, flooded with duplicate ingredients, less easy to use.

reviews.title: Good app with issues
reviews.text: I’ve used the free version of Noom for years and the purchased version at times also. This app is good, but a few things: No where in the settings or profile does it tell you your email that I used to open this account which was probably about 17 years ago). So when I purchased a new phone I couldn’t get logged in without this information. (I’ve used several different emails over the past 20 years). This required me to chat with one of their live agents for them to go find it (by me listing all my past emails). Also I was told by the agent that I must remove the app from my previous phone before I can access it on my new phone. When I asked what is Noom’s solution for customers that lose or break their phone and was told there is nothing they can do about that - our health history data will be lost.   I’m very surprised that an app that has been around this long, hasn’t worked out these simple problems.

reviews.title: App doesn’t work
reviews.text: I’ve created a noom profile 3 freaking times in row. A complete waste of time!! It just takes you right back to the initial intake questionnaire after I try to sign up for the annual plan!

reviews.title: Bait and switch with a poor customer service
reviews.text: I’ve lost so much time and parí dealing with the customer service of this app.  It may be good for physical health, but at the expense of your mental health. Save yourself the aggravation and choose something else

reviews.title: Very helpful!
reviews.text:
My wife and I are both having success with Noom. The lessons really do help us understand our habits and relationship with food, exercise, and sleep. I am down 9 pounds in 10 weeks and my wife is down 6, but the biggest change has been in my outlook on my diet. I’m eating healthier without feeling hungry, I have more energy, and I don’t criticize myself when I have the occasional treat or setback. Thank you!

One suggestion: when logging exercise it would be helpful to list the most common activities a person does at the top. For example, I weightlifting 4-5 days per week and it’s down towards the bottom. A quick tweak but it could be a nice time saver.

reviews.title: BEST DECISION! BEST BRAND/APP!!!
reviews.text: I have PCOS and I am postpartum and have been struggling with my weight due to my hormonal imbalances. Not only did NOOM give me the best pricing for what I needed, they also have the BEST system. The connect you with a doctor and a coach to help you along the way as well as an app that tracks your calories and macros (if you want) as well and makes it fun to keep you engaged. They give you a whole catalog of workouts for any and all of your personal needs and restrictions. Between the pricing, the resources and how easy everything was. 2000/10 for on Noom!!!! These guys did it the best!!!! And trust me I looked at a bunch of different options for GLP-1’s because I read it was good for my PCOS. GO WITH NOOM!! They set you up for success before, during and after the process!

reviews.title: Great accountability and feedback.
reviews.text: I really appreciate the learning model associated with the tracking for goals. The accountability is helpful and fun.

reviews.title: Motivating!
reviews.text: I have tried a lot of different apps but noon is the real deal. Very motivating and I actually stick to it.

reviews.title: Pleasantly Surprised
reviews.text: The program is manageable and adjustable. I don’t feel like I am lacking anything and certainly am not hungry. If anything I am amazed at the amount of food I can eat. I have make things I like and adjusted them slowly to add more vegetables and other healthier options. It makes much more sense to why this sticks and is a lifestyle change and not just another diet.

reviews.title: It’s ok
reviews.text: This review is more about the app itself and less about the program (which is good). Specifically, I am incredibly frustrated with the food tracking. For an app that is intended to encourage habit building, it is incredibly frustrating that there is no way to save individual food items as favorites, or that the algorithm doesn’t at least recognize foods you frequently log and prioritize them in the list of foods. If I eat the same thing every day and have to log it, I don’t want to have to go through the exercise of looking it up EVERY time I log a food item (an individual item, not a meal). It makes me not want to do it at all, which is the exact opposite of what Noom purports to be encouraging. Please make a way to save or favorite items, like literally every other food tracking app out there

reviews.title: Gave them a chance…
reviews.text:
Paid for a plan, completed all my steps.. the site throws in your face the missed appointment fee if the user misses it… yet the user gets nothing when the clinician blows off the appointment and doesn’t show, which is what happened to me. 
Canceled my plan and demanded a refund, will give my money to another source for the same service.

reviews.title: Lots of issues, but some good ideas
reviews.text: I got a free subscription through my clinic.  One week in, and I’m probably going to stop using this app.  The good: the app does a good job of estimating ingredients based on a photo.  However, it really likes to overestimate quantities (two bites of sushi is estimated to contain one cup of rice and two ounces of fish, as one example).  The meal tracking is challenging and very stress-inducing for those of us with atypical schedules.  It allows three meals and three snacks per day, but if I’m switching from days to nights, as often needed for my work, I cannot log things live, as it may require more slots than are available.  Because of this, I’m waiting until the end of my day to log them.  This means incorrect information, particularly not logging large numbers of snacks and meals.  And if that’s a Sunday night shift?  Poof!  The week resets “midday” and I cannot log nor even review it.  Activity logging is weird as well if you’re doing more than letting a device track your steps.  In all, it makes me irritated, hangry, and want to stress eat even more than I can do without it.  I think I’ll try a spreadsheet instead.

reviews.title: Must Have
reviews.text: I have been clueless about how to diet for the long haul. Noom has provided me with the information and encouragement to keep me going. I now have a better understanding of body and mind. I couldn’t do it without Noom.

reviews.title: Just Get a Calorie Counter
reviews.text: Disappointing generic AI suggestions. Inexplicably had my subscription canceled. To apologize, I was “offered” the same discount that got sent out in a targeted email blast which was just insulting. Save yourself the frustration, money, and trouble, and just get a calorie counter.

reviews.title: Bad customer service
reviews.text: If you use this app and buy through Apple Store be prepared for zero customer service. They keep releasing new features but if you buy through the Apple Store they will not give them to you.  1/10.

reviews.title: Progress
reviews.text: Been not gaining so very happy

reviews.title: No reminders before renewal
reviews.text: Please be aware that you will receive NO notification of upcoming renewals. Subscription will renew automatically without warning and you will be surprised by a hefty charge after initial trial period. Extremely unhappy.

reviews.title: Glitch at weight graph in current version
reviews.text: The current version freezes up in the weight graph on an iPhone 16, you can’t zoom out or tap any of the menus it just gets stuck there and you have to close the ap to get out of it

reviews.title: Science meets Support
reviews.text: Great tools, education, and supportive (unforced) community. Addresses the whole picture in a real world way which allows for lasting change rather than another fad diet rebound

reviews.title: Low weight loss
reviews.text:
I lost 5 lbs initially but none for four weeks. I have been slowly increasing my GLP-1 with no difference. Disappointed with Noom plus meds.

Important note, you have to wean off GLP-1 that increases price.

reviews.title: Confusing billing
reviews.text:
I have had Noom for about a month and while the actual app seems pretty good (great, in fact), their billing model is not transparent and if you decide to add premium later, it charges you the entire amount for the base weight loss program and the premium, rather than just the premium separate or in part (since you’ve already paid for the basic). So, for me to upgrade, it appears I’d need to cancel the membership before the three month window and then restart the premium? But even then, there’s not a list of prices (or I might have chosen premium to start with). Anyway, it’s a good app otherwise. I’m writing this review for feedback and I hope they can fix this issue in the future. After chatting with a service person, I decided not to upgrade to premium (because it would charge me an additional $200)

Update: I was finally able to talk to a person in customer service and he finally explained the pricing system and insisted it would not double charge me (I was still doubtful), but he could not add me to the premium on the phone and when I tried to do it myself, I got a notification to call customer support. So…we just won’t do premium. Again, I like the actual app, but the pricing system is not transparent. I added back a star, but still only four stars, due to the pricing confusion and difficulty getting help with billing.

reviews.title: Completely rip off
reviews.text: Difficult to cancel. Hard to use. Doesn’t actually work. Don’t fall for the ads. This app is garbage.

reviews.title: iPad access
reviews.text: The new app is not letting me access everything like I can access it on my iPhone

reviews.title: Got rewarded
reviews.text: Great app. Takes a while to get the reward gift card but but you have to hang in there. I adore the Art break.

reviews.title: Amazing app, but way too expensive
reviews.text: This app is so great and it does what other weight loss apps do but better…but the price is astronomical. I got an email to get 7 months free and “put code in at checkout”…there was no place to put it in at checkout lol. It just gives you a 7 day free trial option. I’m disappointed because the app itself is amazing, and I wish I could use it, but there’s no way I could afford $15 per week.

reviews.title: New updates ruined it
reviews.text: I used to use the free version of Noom to track food intake, but this new version is terrible. I’ll admit I haven’t used it in about 6-8 months so I don’t know when this changed, but not being able to search for food and only using a description or photo is terrible. I tried to look into upgrade options: that’s not working and keeps telling me it’s only for people who want to lose weight. Spent over an hour going in circles with the chatbot who eventually told me to go to the website, gave the wrong directions for what I needed, managed to get in contact with someone who eventually provided links to different subscription packages and they are unfortunately way out of my price range.

reviews.title: Noom is awesome!
reviews.text:
Very happy with the app to help track everything and more! 
Doctor and staff is very helpful and informative. I used to see a nutritionist and I feel like Noom is way better for the busy schedule person.

reviews.title: Noom works!
reviews.text: I did Noom for a year, even though I lost my weight in 4 months. When the year ended, I took a break, but I missed knowing how healthy my meals were or how many calories I was burning. I just missed it, so I went back!  The new version has 2 weekly minutes of art, which I do not enjoy, but I am hoping they will soon make that optional. That is why I gave it 4 stars, not 5 - the dang art.

reviews.title: Fraudulent charge
reviews.text: Noom offered a short trial with a promise to remind before the trial period expired.  No such reminder ever occurred so I was charged for the initial.  If you sign up for a trial, be sure to cancel immediately so you aren’t charged without consent.

reviews.title: Auto-renewed without notice
reviews.text: When I went to cancel the subscription earlier in the year, I was given an extension if I kept the account. Then I was charged for the subscription as an to-renewal with no notice. Vary shady practice.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: I like this app. The program is good and it’s based on research. If you stick with it, you’ll lose weight. Things I don’t like: 1. The program is expensive to go from the free app to the supported app subscription and you don’t get a lot for it. Mine was $200 and what I got was access to recipes and community. They say that there is a coach BOT. 2. It’s difficult to get support if you need it. The AI will try to help you and it is often wrong. getting to an actual person was hard. I wouldn’t recommend this subscription unless you’re getting the premium subscription and which case you get more help.

reviews.title: I love this app
reviews.text: I love using the app! I love tracking meals and reading the lessons. Very helpful way to get healthy and retrain my brain.

reviews.title: Body scan never works
reviews.text: I have tried with using just data, with WiFi on , I even tried someone else's wifi, and the body scans are not working. The first two worked fine, but it's been over a month with these issues. Super frustrating.

reviews.title: My program
reviews.text: At first the sign up was confusing to me.  I actually ordered the wrong program. Had to cancel and rejoin.

reviews.title: Let me edit/view yesterday!
reviews.text:
For whatever reason someone decided that the newest update should not allow users to go back to the previous day (or any previous days) to view or edit any food logging, and I find that preposterous. I want to view my journey, see my progress, take note of positive or negative changes in my diet, even just update when I forget an item, why is that something that’s been removed? 

Also, my day lasts as long as I’m awake. When I’m awake right now at 12:41am on a Monday, I still am counting towards Sunday. So not being able to view or edit Sunday is extremely frustrating and screws up my progress. I must now take a screenshot before midnight of any unused calories and just figure it out on my own after midnight, and I can’t log anything new I’ve eaten unless I want it to count towards the current day (and I don’t). 

Please change this back immediately or someone justify why not being able to view or edit prior days’ food logging is actually a benefit. My rating remains 1 star until this is fixed. Otherwise it would be 5 stars.

reviews.title: Sham
reviews.text: When I first started I was losing 2 pounds a week as advertised. Then they changed my doctor without my permission and changed the manufacturer of my medication. I can tell that the product I was now getting was different than the original bc it stopped working. I was not nauseous anymore but I was still tired. Most importantly, I stopped losing weight. I was on a weight loss plateau for 7 months and I’m pretty sure they did that to waste my time and my money. The fatigue and the harm this med does to the organs over time was not worth money I was wasting just to not lose any weight. I’m frustrated as hell bc I feel like I keep getting targeted by these schemes for my money to be wasted, but I’m trying something else. These doctors are useless and refuse to help me. They just watch me struggle.

reviews.title: Noom has lost its way
reviews.text: Having used the app a few years ago pre-menopause, I’ve been disappointed with the return. The substitution of points for community and nutrition support is a distraction. Points do not equal weight loss. Instead it serves as a distraction. The normal Noom app should offer menopause recommendations even if you are not taking hormones. Keeping 2 stars bc it’s still a decent food tracker. Lose the points or offer an option to turn them off. Regular plan should include recommendations for menopause. The degradations in quality reflect the leadership team - dudes without a clue.

reviews.title: Not for menopausal women
reviews.text: I tried this app for a year. I bought the subscription for one year and I logged in everything. I just fluctuated between 162 lbs and 165 lbs for an entire year no matter what I ate. This app did not work for me at all.
